main_body: Seamless dark grey-brown cobble/rivet-like ground texture patch filling the whole canvas (terrain tile, not a standing object)
top_band: none (flat terrain texture; the column scan shows repeating cobble rows, no standing top surface)
evidence: Terrain kind: a ground paving texture of repeating rounded stones in a brick-like pattern. It is not a standing object, so the top/front contract does not apply. No isometric side faces and no container or opening are drawn. The column scan shows a periodic pattern of dark and mid-tone runs, as expected for a tiled ground surface.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours in the whole piece and a median of 5 per tile, against 26 per tile and 80 colours for the grass reference. The paving reference is close to it at 7 colours per tile and 7 distinct colours. Dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, so the dark lines are a neutral grey-black with no material tint, which is the sticker look. The paving reference has 80% neutral, so it is not far off. The stones are repeated with identical highlights and no per-stone variation, and the ramp has only 5 steps versus the references' 7. There are no flat fills (0% coverage). The overall look is a uniform stamped pattern, thinner and more mechanical than the Beodeul paving, which shows individual stone shading and lighter mortar highlights. Judged against the references, this is shallower in steps, colour count and texture variety.
